item.title: CARMEN.maquia Ballet Hispanico — Feb 4, 2027
item.description: Lied Center Main Stage Thursday, February 4, 2027 · 7:30 PM Bizet's Carmen has seen countless interpretations over the past 150 years, but never one like this. Acclaimed choreographer Gustavo Ramrez Sansano brings this full-length ballet to the stage, inspired by tauromaquia - the art of bullfighting - breathing a modern life into this legendary character. Highly original and full of explosive movement that leaves you breathless, CARMEN.maquiais a bold reimagining of this tragic tale presented by Ballet Hispnico New York, the nation's leading Hispanic/Latin dance company. Source: Lied Center for Performing Arts

item.title: Orpheus Chamber Orchestra — Feb 17, 2027
item.description: Lied Center Main Stage Wednesday, February 17, 2027 · 7:30 PM GRAMMY® award-winning Orpheus Chamber Orchestra returns to the Lied with British virtuoso pianist Isata Kanneh-Mason for an evening of elegance and vitality. The program pairs classical favorites by Mozart and Haydn with selections from Handel's Water Music Suite and a newly commissioned work by Katie Jenkins, showcasing Orpheus' trademark conductor-less precision and collaborative spirit. Source: Lied Center for Performing Arts

item.title: Piano Battle — Mar 20, 2027
item.description: Lied Center Main Stage Saturday, March 20, 2027 · 7:30 PM It's classical music like you've never seen it before! In Piano Battle, virtuoso pianists Andreas Kern and Paul Cibis go head-to-head in a thrilling, interactive competition where the audience decides the winner of each round. Blending dazzling technique with humor and showmanship, this high-energy performance transforms a traditional recital into an unforgettable musical showdown. Who performs it best? You decide! Source: Lied Center for Performing Arts

item.title: Daniil Trifonov — Mar 22, 2027
item.description: Lied Center Main Stage Monday, March 22, 2027 · 7:30 PM Praised as "the most astounding pianist of our age" by London's The Times, GRAMMY® Award-winning pianist Daniil Trifonov makes his Lied Center debut with a program showcasing extraordinary range. Handel's Suite No. 5 in E Major ("The Harmonious Blacksmith") opens the concert followed by Stravinsky's sole piano sonata and Schubert's beloved "Wanderer Fantasy," a powerful musical depiction of a stranger's search for meaning and happiness in a strange land. Trifonov's stylistic exploration continues on the program's second half featuring Brazilian, Argentine, and Dominican composers as well as his own original Tango! Combining consummate technique with rare sensitivity and depth, Trifonov's performances are a perpetual source of wonder to audiences and critics alike. Source: Lied Center for Performing Arts
